items.text: The catch block now awaits an unguarded prisma.workflowReminder.update which can throw (P2025 when row was deleted concurrently), causing the error to escape the for loop, skipping remaining reminders and the original error log
Reminders that continue because workflowStep/booking is missing or have no message/sendTo are never counted, so the retry cap does not cover every path where a reminder is never scheduled

retryCount is incremented by read-modify-write from a stale in-memory value (reminder.retryCount + 1) instead of using Prisma's atomic { increment: 1 }, causing overlapping cron runs to lose increments
`update()` will throw if the reminder was deleted between `findMany` and this write, which would escape the catch block - needs to be robust to concurrency and missing rows
The identical retryCount update block is duplicated in the else branch (178-187) and in the catch (189-197)
The select spread plus ad-hoc cast `as (PartialWorkflowReminder & { retryCount: number })[]` exists only to read retryCount for manual increment and widens the shared type at the call site

The retryCount is incremented using the stale in-memory value (reminder.retryCount + 1) rather than an atomic database operation. If this cron handler runs concurrently or the same reminder is processed twice, both executions read the same retryCount and write the same incremented value, losing one update. Should use Prisma's atomic increment instead: retryCount: { increment: 1 }

Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

retryCount is read, modified and written back from a stale in-memory value (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) instead of using Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }`, causing lost increments if two cron runs overlap

In scheduleSMSReminders, the catch block calls prisma.workflowReminder.update() to increment retryCount, but that update can throw if the reminder was deleted concurrently, escaping the catch and aborting the entire cron run

The Twilio provider API call and database persistence are in a single try-catch, so if Twilio accepts the SMS but the database update fails, the error is treated as a send failure causing duplicate SMS on retry

Using JavaScript-level addition (reminder.retryCount + 1) instead of Prisma's atomic increment operator creates race conditions when two scheduler instances run concurrently, causing one failure to be lost and weakening the delete after two failures logic
No test covers the new branches: increment on a falsy result, increment on throw, delete at the threshold, and no increment on success
After multiple database failures, the reminder row may be deleted leaving orphaned jobs on Twilio with no database reference
`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` is based on a potentially stale in-memory value; if this cron overlaps/runs concurrently it can lose increments

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
No tests cover the new behaviour: increment on falsy result, increment on throw, deletion at threshold, and no increment on success

The deleteMany OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` (lines 38-42) has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, causing the SMS cron to potentially delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows whose retryCount > 1
The second OR branch in the deleteMany query is missing a method guard, so it will delete any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, not just SMS reminders - the cleanup should be scoped to SMS only

Reminders for SMS-locked or rate-limited users and teams are now counted as failures and permanently deleted after two cron runs, whereas before they stayed queued until scheduledDate and could still send once the lock was lifted or the limit reset

retryCount is added by spreading the shared select and widening an ad-hoc cast to `(PartialWorkflowReminder & { retryCount: number })[]` at the call site, instead of extending the type and select in getWorkflowReminders.ts

The `retryCount > 1` branch isn't scoped to `method: SMS`, so it will delete any WorkflowReminder that happens to have retryCount incremented (even non-SMS methods), causing potential unintended data loss

The second OR branch in the deleteMany query deletes ANY WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method type, because it lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing non-SMS reminders (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) to be unintentionally deleted by the SMS cron job
The `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ where: { id }, data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } })` block is duplicated in the else branch (:178-187) and the catch (:189-197)
The retry-count cleanup is not scoped to SMS reminders. As written, any reminder with retryCount > 1 will be deleted, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows
The WhatsApp cron uses the same twilio.scheduleSMS path and has the same retry-forever problem but does not get the retry count even though the column now exists on every WorkflowReminder

Reminders for SMS-locked or rate-limited users are counted as failures and deleted after two runs instead of staying queued - scheduleSMS returns undefined when isLockedForSMSSending which hits the else-branch increment, and checkSMSRateLimit throws which hits the catch increment
The catch block awaits an unguarded `prisma.workflowReminder.update` - if that update throws, the error escapes the for loop, skipping remaining reminders and the original error's console.log
The comment 'delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date' no longer describes the query, which now also deletes rows with retryCount > 1

The prisma.workflowReminder.update in the catch block (line 191) is unprotected - if it throws (e.g., the record was already deleted by the deleteMany above, or a DB connection issue), the error propagates out of the for...of loop and halts processing of all remaining reminders. Wrap this update in a nested try-catch or append .catch() to prevent a single failure from stopping the entire cron job.

The new OR branch { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } is not scoped to method SMS or scheduled:false, so the SMS cron would delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders and already-scheduled ones once anything else increments retryCount

Any failure (transient or permanent) counts toward deletion - two consecutive failed cron runs set retryCount to 2, and the next run's deleteMany permanently removes every unscheduled SMS reminder in the 7-day window with no backoff or distinction between permanent and transient errors

issues.claim: The catch block awaits an unguarded prisma.workflowReminder.update to increment retryCount. That update can throw, for example P2025 when the row was deleted concurrently or by the earlier deleteMany. The error then escapes the for loop, which skips the remaining reminders and the original error log and aborts the cron run.

retryCount is incremented by read-modify-write from the stale in-memory value (reminder.retryCount + 1) instead of Prisma's atomic { increment: 1 }. Overlapping or concurrent cron runs therefore lose increments.
The identical prisma.workflowReminder.update retryCount block is duplicated in the else branch (lines 178-187) and in the catch block (lines 189-197).

retryCount is read by spreading the shared select and casting ad hoc to (PartialWorkflowReminder & { retryCount: number })[] at the call site. The type and select in getWorkflowReminders.ts are not extended.

The deleteMany OR branch { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } has no method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter (and no scheduled:false filter). The SMS cron therefore deletes EMAIL, WHATSAPP and already-scheduled WorkflowReminder rows with retryCount > 1.
No tests cover the new branches: increment on a falsy result, increment on throw, deletion at the threshold, and no increment on success.

Reminders for SMS-locked or rate-limited users and teams are counted as failures and deleted after two cron runs. scheduleSMS returns undefined when isLockedForSMSSending, which hits the else-branch increment, and checkSMSRateLimit throws, which hits the catch increment. Previously these reminders stayed queued until scheduledDate.

Reminders skipped via continue because workflowStep or booking is missing, or because they have no message or sendTo, never have retryCount incremented. The retry cap therefore does not cover every path where a reminder is not scheduled.
The Twilio API call and the database persistence share one try-catch. A database update failure after Twilio accepted the SMS is treated as a send failure, which causes a duplicate SMS on retry.
After repeated database failures the reminder row can be deleted while its job is still scheduled on Twilio, leaving orphaned Twilio jobs with no database reference.
The WhatsApp cron uses the same twilio.scheduleSMS path and has the same retry-forever problem, but it does not use retryCount even though the column exists on every WorkflowReminder.
The comment 'delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date' no longer matches the query, which now also deletes rows with retryCount > 1.

Every failure, transient or permanent, counts toward deletion. Two failed cron runs set retryCount to 2, and the next run's deleteMany removes the unscheduled SMS reminder with no backoff and no distinction between transient and permanent errors.
